subject: Dedicated footprint vetting — stress profile and SLA knob mapping
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cho <ethan.cho@lunartech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated footprint vetting — stress profile and SLA knob mapping

Hi Ethan — great to connect yesterday. To scope a Dedicated (reserved GPU) plan that matches LunarTech's expected traffic shape and SLA expectations, can you confirm the items below and attach a small sample of real traffic (CSV is fine):

- Typical and peak concurrent sessions (sessions that hold a KV cache)
- Average prompt tokens and average generated tokens for the LLM features you plan to run (per endpoint)
- Percentiles for response length (p50/p90/p99) if available
- Daily QPS and expected peak QPS window(s) and duration (e.g., 3x daily spikes at 4-6PM PT)
- Target latency SLOs (p95 and p99) for interactive endpoints and acceptable tail latency
- Burst tolerances: how much short-term burst over sustained throughput is acceptable?
- Session affinity / long-lived sessions (yes/no) and average session duration
- Model family you expect to use (e.g., Llama 2 13B q4, Mistral x, etc.)
- Data retention and KV-cache reuse expectations (do you need persistent caches across requests?)
- Any constraints (region, VPC-only deployment, SOC2/PCI requirements)

I attached a short CSV template (redwood_traffic_template.csv) — filling that out will make our sizing runfast. Also, if you have representative prompt examples (anonymized is fine) that’ll help us estimate token mix and batching effects.

Proposed next steps: you share the sample + desired SLOs, our pre-sales engineering team (Marissa) will run a stress-profile synthesis and deliver a short sizing memo with recommended GPU SKUs, estimated reserved capacity, and fallback routing options. Can we aim to have the sample by EOD next Tuesday?

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jul 30, 2025 at 10:15 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Ethan — great to connect yesterday. To scope a Dedicated (reserved GPU) plan that matches LunarTech's expected traffic shape and SLA expectations, can you confirm the items below and attach a small sample of real traffic (CSV is fine):

Thanks Sean — appreciate the checklist. Attached is a small sample (lunartech_traffic_sample.csv) from last week's staging traffic (anonymized). High-level answers below:

- Typical concurrent sessions: 1,200 users, peak concurrent sessions: ~4,800 (30-min peak window during US business hours)
- Average prompt tokens: 45; average generated tokens: 210
- Response length percentiles (approx): p50=150 tokens, p90=380 tokens, p99=1,100 tokens
- Daily QPS: baseline 600 QPS, peak short spikes up to 2,500 QPS for ~20 minutes, rare extended spikes up to 3,200 QPS for <5 minutes during feature launches
- Target latency SLOs: interactive endpoints p95 < 280ms, p99 < 600ms; batch endpoints higher is fine
- Burst tolerance: we can tolerate a 2.5x short-term oversubscription for up to 15 minutes if you provide graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model or queueing)
- Session affinity: yes — we maintain per-user KV cache for context; average session lifespan ~18 minutes
- Model family: primary is Mistral 8x/13B family (quantized variants), fallback to Llama 2 13B if capacity constrained
- Retention: KV cache persistence per session only; no long-term persistence beyond session lifetime (default eviction after 30 minutes)
- Constraints: prefer us-west region; SOC2 is in progress — will share SOC2 contact if needed

We can make the engineering team available for a short 30m walkthrough of the CSV later this week. Priya (cc'd) will coordinate timing.

— Ethan
Ethan Cho
Head of Platform, LunarTech
ethan.cho@lunartech.ai | +1 650-555-0199

Attachments: lunartech_traffic_sample.csv (anonymized staging traffic sample)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated footprint vetting — stress profile and SLA knob mapping

Thanks for the fast turnaround, Ethan — this is great. Quick clarifying questions before we start the sizing run:

- For the p99 values you gave (1,100 tokens), can you confirm whether that includes multi-step generation (i.e., multiple inference calls per user action) or is that single-call output? If multi-call, please give per-call histograms.
- Do you expect any significant increases in average generated tokens during holiday promotions / feature launches that would push sustained response lengths +50% for >1 hour?
- For the KV cache: do you pin embeddings or serialized context per session, or is it purely LLM KV (keys/values)? This affects estimated GPU memory pressure.

Operational note: we'll run two sizing scenarios — (A) optimistic with higher KV cache compression and (B) conservative assuming full KV retention per session. We'll include recommended GPU SKUs (e.g., A100 80GB, H100 80GB, or an M60 mix depending on quantized model fit), an occupancy curve for sustained vs. burst, and a suggested fallback routing policy (e.g., model downshift + rate-limit gating).

Sean — can you confirm LunarTech's preferred contact for SOC2 evidence once they need it? I'll add the SOC2 person to the loop only when required.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Pre-Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
